public_use_case: A team holding a large model artifact (GGUF or Safetensors, hundreds of GB to TB-scale, hosted behind plain HTTP) needs questions answered about its weights - tensor health, embedding geometry, baked circuits, quantization stress, precision recipe - without downloading, storing, or GPU-evaluating the whole file. Commons WB-RANGE reads addressed byte ranges over HTTP Range requests and runs an 80+ metric pure-stdlib union on the decoded slices, so fulfillment cost is bandwidth-scale instead of storage- and compute-scale.

source_side.description: Commons WB-RANGE capability on woahwhattheheck/commons main: host/wb_range.py (Range reader, header-only GGUF/Safetensors index, row/span fetch, metric dispatch, control panel) plus host/wb_metrics.py (pure-stdlib metric union), landed via PRs #5317, #5318, #5320. Measured 2026-08-29 against moonshotai/Kimi-K3 (1.56 TB Safetensors, 96 shards): header-only index then addressed range reads ran a live 11-op metric battery (anisotropy, axis purity, analogy battery, category purity, bit-depth, mechanism, concept neighbors, circuitry, precision recipe, tensor stats) with KB-scale fetches per operation; one embedding-row-class read fetched ~14 KB against the 1.56 TB total. Marginal cash cost is bandwidth only; USD 1.00 is carried as a conservative per-engagement allowance.
